purpose: Teach: ジュン/純一郎/愛子/めぐみ/幸子/直樹/哲也/ディック

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがお孫様にジュンと愛称を付けられた
lines.en: You know, Gran — when I was young, my father gave my grandson the nickname Jun.
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward into memory. Pause after 'Gran' — searching. Warm but distant, like the memory itself is fading even as he speaks it. Voice settles on the name.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、小泉純一郎元首相を尊敬されてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm, that's right — you really admired Prime Minister Koizumi, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle correction wrapped in affection. 'Admired' lands with knowing warmth — she's testing his memory, tenderly. The 'dear' at the end is a small anchor, keeping him tethered to the present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが皇室の愛子様の御誕生を喜ばれた
lines.en: Gran — when I was young, my father was so glad when Princess Aiko was born.
lines.style: Same wistful distance. Slight lift on 'was born' — a moment of brightness breaking through. Still looking inward, not at her. The memory carries quiet joy.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お友達のめぐみさんと文通されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Dear, when you were young, you used to write letters to your friend Megumi, didn't you?
lines.style: Playful curiosity. She's sparring gently — offering him a memory she knows is real. 'Write letters' has a tender specificity. The question lands as invitation, not interrogation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが妹の幸子さんを慈しまれた
lines.en: Gran — when I was young, my father was so fond of my sister Sachiko.
lines.style: Voice softens on 'sister.' The affection is old and settled. Slight breathiness — he's moved by it still. Quieter than before, almost to himself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ご友人の直樹さんと釣りに行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Dear, when you were young, you went fishing with your friend Naoki, didn't you?
lines.style: She's weaving the pattern now — matching his rhythm. 'Fishing' carries the ease of memory. Voice has the rhythm of a call-and-response, almost sung. Small smile underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと哲也さんの父上が同僚だった
lines.en: Gran — when I was young, my father and Tetsuya's father were colleagues.
lines.style: Simpler now, almost factual. But the simplicity is tender — he's not reaching for emotion, just letting it sit. Shorter breath. The detail of 'colleagues' settles like a bookmark.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、米国の音楽家ディック・デールの曲を愛されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Dear, you loved that American musician Dick Dale's songs, didn't you?
lines.style: This one lands softer, warmer — a final turn of the key. Her voice carries both question and affirmation. 'Loved' is genuine. The 'dear' feels like she's bringing him home.
